# Config files

Every file termocode reads or writes. termocode never fails to start because of a missing or broken file; it uses defaults instead.

## Config folder

`~/.config/termocode/`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/termocode/`.

| File | Purpose | Format | Safe to edit? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config.json` | Settings (theme, editor, search, AI). See the settings reference. | JSON object. Unknown keys are kept on save. | Yes. Also Preferences: Open Settings (UI). |
| `keymap.json` | Key binding overrides. See the keys reference. | JSON object: key string → action name, or `"ext:<command id>"` for an extension command. | Yes. Also Preferences: Customize Keybindings. |
| `commands.json` | User commands shown in the palette as `User: <title>`. | JSON array of `{"id", "title", "cmd", "cwd"}`. | Yes. Open with Open Config: User Commands. |
| `snippets.json` | User snippets, layered over the built-in ones. | JSON object: scope (filetype or `*`) → trigger → body (string or array of lines). | Yes. Also Snippets: Manage…. |
| `user_theme.json` | Custom color theme saved by the theme editor. | JSON object: palette key (for example `BgEditor`) → hex color. Used by the `custom` theme. | Yes, but Preferences: Edit Custom Theme is easier. |
| `breakpoints.json` | Saved debugger breakpoints per file (line and line text). | JSON `{"version", "breakpoints": {file: [...]}}`. | Not needed. termocode rewrites it when breakpoints change. |
| `sessions/<hash>.json` | Session of one workspace: open files, tab order, cursor positions, expanded folders, extra workspace roots, last AI chat. The name is a hash of the workspace path; the `workspace` key says which folder. | JSON, written by termocode. | No (state). Developer: Reset Session clears the current workspace's file and keeps a `.bak`. |
| `session.json` | Layout kept across all workspaces: terminal height, Actions panel, Source Control view. A session.json from before per-workspace sessions moves to `sessions/` the first time its workspace opens. | JSON, written by termocode. | No (state). Safe to delete. |
| `recents.json` | Recent files for the welcome screen and File: Open Recent…. | JSON array. | No (state). Safe to delete. |
| `workspaces.json` | Recent workspace folders for File: Open Recent Workspace…. | JSON array. | No (state). Safe to delete. |
| `palette_recents.json` | Recently used palette commands (shown first). | JSON array of command IDs. | No (state). Safe to delete. |
| `errors.log` | Log of error and warning toasts. `tail -f` it while debugging. | Plain text, one timestamped line per entry; secrets are redacted. | Safe to delete. |
| `settings-backup-<time>.json` | Backup written before Preferences: Import termocode Settings File…. | Settings bundle (same shape as an export). | Safe to delete. |
| `extensions/<name>/` | Lua extensions: `extension.json` manifest and `init.lua`. | Folder per extension. | Yes. Extensions: New Extension… creates one. |
| `secrets.json` | Index of your saved secrets: each name, whether it is a value or a reference, the backend in use and when it changed. It never holds a secret value, only names and reference text such as `${env:NAME}`. | JSON `{"version", "backend": "keyring"\|"age"\|"plain", "entries": {name: {"kind", "ref", "backend", "updated"}}}`. | Not needed. Use AI: Secret Store… to see and forget names. |
| `secrets.age` | Your secrets in an encrypted file (age, passphrase), used when there is no OS keyring, for example over SSH or on Termux. File mode 0600. termocode asks for the passphrase once while it runs. | One age file holding a JSON object `{name: value}`. Binary, not for editing. | No. Back it up with care: without the passphrase it can not be read. |
| `web/devices.json` | The phones and tablets paired with the web panel (Web: Pair a Device…): name, role, and the passkey's public key and counter. No secret: a public key cannot sign in. File mode 0600 (folder 0700). | JSON `{"version", "devices": [{"id", "name", "role", "guest", "cred_id", "public_key", "sign_count", "user_id", "rp_id", "created", "last_seen"}]}`. | Use Web: Devices… to remove one. Delete the file to forget every device. |
| `ai/credentials.json` | The old plain secret file: AI API keys, Claude OAuth tokens, MCP secrets and MCP sign-ins, not encrypted. File mode 0600 (folder 0700). Used only while secret_store is plain, or until AI: Move Secrets to a Safer Store… moves it to the OS keyring or secrets.age; the file is deleted only after you confirm on a card. | JSON `{"keys": {provider: key}, "claude_oauth": {...}, "mcp_secrets": {name: value}, "mcp_oauth": {server: {issuer, resource, tokens…, account}}, "mcp_accounts": {server: account}}`. | With care. Prefer AI: Configure Provider…. Never exported by Preferences: Export termocode Settings File…. |
| `ai/credentials.json.migrated` | Empty marker written after the secrets were moved out of ai/credentials.json. While it exists termocode does not offer the move again. | Empty file, mode 0600. | Yes. Delete it to be asked again when a plain ai/credentials.json comes back. |
| `ai/profiles.json` | Your agent profiles: named pipelines of AI steps (built in: default, review, fast, local-only, plan; yours win by name, except default). | JSON `{"profiles": {name: {"title", "categories": {"quick"\|"deep": slot}, "budget_usd", "steps": [{"id", "title", "slot", "category", "system", "tools": {"preset": "none"\|"read-only"\|"all", "allow", "deny"}, "output": "shown"\|"folded"\|"hidden", "max_steps", "deps", "plan", "cli", "provider", "model"}]}}}`. At most 12 steps, system prompts up to 8 KB; `deps` needs ai_parallel_max 2 or more; at most one `plan` step; `budget_usd` pauses a run at that cost. Slots come from ai_models in config.json; a step with `provider` + `model` needs no slot; no keys in this file. | Yes. A broken file is skipped (the built-in profiles stay) and the error names the line. |
| `ai/providers.json` | The AIs you connected, one per provider kind: how (an API key in the secret store, a CLI's own sign-in, a server on this machine, a server URL) and where. Profile steps with `provider` take the server URL from here. Without the file, termocode reads the list from your setup (stored keys, ai_provider). | JSON `{"providers": {kind: {"method": "key"\|"cli"\|"local"\|"url", "cli", "base_url", "title", "added_at"}}}`. No keys or passwords: a `base_url` with a user or password is refused. Unknown keys are kept. | Yes. An entry with an unknown kind or method is skipped. |
| `ai/chats/*.json` | Saved AI chats (newest 50 kept). | JSON, one file per chat. | Safe to delete. |
| `mcp.json` | Your MCP servers: their tools are offered to the AI chat. See the MCP guide. | The shape other apps write: `{"mcpServers": {name: {"command", "args", "env", "cwd"}}}` for local servers, `{"type": "http", "url", "headers"}` for remote ones, plus `readOnly`, `autoApprove`, `deny`, `timeout`, `disabled`, `oauth` (`client_id`, `client_secret`, `scopes` of a pre-registered app) and `auth` (`{"gh": "<login>"}`: the token comes from the GitHub CLI; only in this file, not in a project's). Secrets as `${secret:NAME}` (from your secret store) or `${VAR}`. | Yes. Open with Open Config: MCP Servers. |
| `db/history.jsonl` | Redacted SQL history, capped at 4 KB per entry; mode 0600. | JSON lines; db_history_max trims the list. | Databases: History… → Clear history…. |
| `db/consoles/` | SQL consoles per workspace and connection, mode 0600. | SQL with a -- @conn <id> header. | Yes. Press n on a database connection. |
| `http/saved.http` | Requests saved with HTTP: Save Request to Saved… (S on the response page). | A normal `.http` file (the format mobocode reads too). File mode 0600. | Yes. HTTP: Saved Requests… → Open saved.http. |
| `http/history.jsonl` | HTTP history: one JSON line per send (yours and the AI's). Holds the request as written (`{{templates}}`, secret headers `[REDACTED]`), never the resolved values; the first 256 KB of a text answer. File mode 0600, folder 0700. | JSON lines, written by termocode; `http_history_max` trims it. | No (state). HTTP: History… → Clear history…, or delete it. |
| `http/state.json` | The HTTP environment chosen per workspace (HTTP: Select Environment…). | JSON `{"envs": {workspace: env}}`. | Not needed. |

## Data folder

`~/.local/share/termocode/`, or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/termocode/`.

| File | Purpose | Format | Safe to edit? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins/` | Neovim plugins cloned in the background on first launch (nvim-dap, vim-visual-multi, rainbow-delimiters). | Git checkouts. `$TERMOCODE_PLUGINS_DIR` moves it. | Delete to re-clone on next launch. |
| `tools/` | Language servers and debug adapters installed by LSP: Manage Language Servers… and DAP: Install Adapter…. | One folder per tool; `tools/bin` holds shims on Neovim's PATH. `$TERMOCODE_TOOLS_DIR` moves it. | Use the palette commands. Delete a tool folder to remove it. |
| `tools/asked.json` | Filetypes already asked about in the "no language server" toast. | JSON `{"filetypes": [...]}`. | Safe to delete (the toasts come back). |

## Workspace folder

Inside the folder you open.

| File | Purpose | Format | Safe to edit? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.termocode/tasks.json` | Workspace tasks for Tasks: Run Task…. | VS Code style tasks: `label`, `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `env`, `group`, `problemMatcher`. | Yes. Tasks: Configure Tasks creates it. |
| `.termocode/services.json` | Local dev services for the Services view (and the compose file / profiles to use). | JSONC: `compose` {`file`, `profiles`, `project`}, `services` [{`name`, `command`, `cwd`, `env`, `port`, `health` {`tcp` \| `http`}}]. | Yes. Containers: Configure Services creates it. A local command asks once before its first start. |
| `.termocode/launch.json` | Debug and run configurations. | VS Code `launch.json` shape; comments allowed. | Yes. Debug: Open launch.json creates it. |
| `.mcp.json` | Project MCP servers in the common file other apps read too. Read before .termocode/mcp.json, which wins on a name clash. | Same shape as the user mcp.json. | Yes. Same trust question as .termocode/mcp.json; `${cmd:}`, `auth.gh` and a `headersCommand` are refused. |
| `.termocode/mcp.json` | Project MCP servers. An entry with the same name as one in your mcp.json replaces it; `"disabled": true` hides it in this project. | Same shape as the user mcp.json. | Yes. termocode asks before it starts a project server the first time (and again when the entry changes). |
| `.termocode/ai-profiles.json` | Project agent profiles. A profile with the same name as one of yours replaces it in this project. | Same shape as ai/profiles.json; a `models` key is ignored (a project can not point you at another server). | Yes. A broken file is skipped and the error names the line. |
| `AGENTS.md` | Project rules for the AI chat: they go into its system prompt (see Project rules file in the Use AI guide). | Plain text or Markdown; at most 16 KB (together with .termocode/rules.md) is used. | Yes. termocode asks once per workspace before it uses the rules, and again when the text changes. |
| `.termocode/rules.md` | More project rules for the AI chat, after AGENTS.md when both exist. | Same as AGENTS.md. | Yes. Same question as AGENTS.md. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Project rules for the AI chat, read like AGENTS.md. In a sub folder (also AGENTS.md there) they apply to the files below it and are added when the AI reads one. | Same as AGENTS.md; at most 4 KB of a folder file is added per read. | Yes. Same question as AGENTS.md. |
| `.claude/rules/*.md` | Rules for some files: `globs:` or `paths:` in the front matter choose the files; `alwaysApply: true` (or no front matter) puts them in the system prompt. | Markdown or .mdc with an optional `---` front matter. | Yes. Same question as AGENTS.md. |
| `.termocode/memory/lessons.md` | AI memory: lessons the AI wrote after earlier chats in this project (see Memory in the Use AI guide). | Markdown; one `## <date> · <title> {#id}` section per lesson, an optional `paths:` line; at most 200 lessons and 64 KB. | Yes. Written only after you turn memory on; AI: Memory… lists and forgets lessons. termocode adds `.termocode/memory/` to .gitignore. |
| `.editorconfig` | Indent and whitespace rules, read by Neovim's EditorConfig support. | EditorConfig INI. | Yes (read only for termocode). |
| `http-client.env.json` | HTTP environments for `{{name}}` in `.http` files, next to them or in a parent folder up to the workspace root (the nearest wins). `$shared` applies to every environment. | JSON `{"$shared": {...}, "dev": {"host": "…"}, …}` (VS Code REST Client / JetBrains shape). | Yes. HTTP: Open Environment File creates it. |
| `http-client.private.env.json` | Secret values (tokens) for the same environments; they win over http-client.env.json, are hidden from the AI and the logs, and must stay out of git. | Same shape as http-client.env.json. | Yes. HTTP: Open Private Environment File creates it (mode 0600) and offers to add it to .gitignore. |

## Other files

| File | Purpose | Format | Safe to edit? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `~/termocode-settings.json` | Default target of Preferences: Export termocode Settings File…. | Settings bundle: `{"termocode_settings": 1, "files": {...}}`. State files and secrets are left out. | Yes, but re-export is easier. |
| `~/.local/share/fonts/JetBrainsMonoNF/` | Nerd Font installed by `termocode setup` (Linux). | Font files. | Safe to delete. |
| `~/.docker/config.json` | Registry hosts and credential helper names for the Containers view's REGISTRIES section (`$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json`; Podman: `$REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE` or `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json`). termocode reads host and helper names only, never the stored logins, and never writes it. | The engine's own JSON (`auths`, `credsStore`, `credHelpers`). | Yes, with `docker login` / `docker logout`; read only for termocode. |
| `~/.cache/termocode/mcp/<name>.tools.json` | Tool list of each MCP server, so a chat turn does not start the server just to list its tools. `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` moves it. | JSON, written by termocode; keyed by a hash of the server's mcp.json entry. | Safe to delete. |

**Preferences: Export termocode Settings File…** writes all config-folder JSON files into one bundle, except state files (`session.json`, `recents.json`, `workspaces.json`, `palette_recents.json`) and anything that looks like a secret.
